summary: Beyond the Signal is a bilingual (Vietnamese/English) digital museum that tells the stories of NASA machines left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space (Opportunity, Pioneer 11, Surveyor 3, Viking 1 and Sojourner) for school-age space enthusiasts. Instead of listing specifications, each machine is told as a journey from launch to silent legacy, backed by a verified timeline, interactive challenges and a source-linked data catalogue built from NASA mission pages, technical reports and official imagery. Two original story products, a comic about Surveyor 3 and a song about Opportunity, making this history personal. Students mostly hear about active missions; these retired explorers made today's discoveries possible.
details:
The challenge: Students usually hear about active missions, while the history of NASA hardware left on the Moon, Mars and in deep space sits in technical archives. Our goal is to turn that history into a story-driven learning experience that connects how a machine was built with what humanity learned from it.
How it works: Beyond the Signal is a web museum (Vietnamese and English), open to everyone without registration.

– Journeys: each machine is told in chapters from launch to its silent legacy, with a verified mission timeline, an accessible audio story with transcript, and an illustrated story.

– Challenges and simulations: short engineering problems built on real mission facts, such as why rovers cannot be driven with a joystick (signal delay), how a passive lunar mirror measures distance, how long a spacecraft can power itself, and a timeline reconstruction that corrects common myths about Surveyor 3, Viking 1 and Sojourner.

– Science data catalogue: machines, instruments, five original NASA technical reports on Surveyor 3, a curated library of official NASA images, and a list of verified references.

– 3D models are shown only where a NASA model exists; printable posters and a young explorers gallery are included.

Story products: (1) a comic about Surveyor 3, the first lander to touch the lunar soil and show it could support the Apollo lunar module; (2) "Little Wheels", a song about Opportunity's 5,111 sols on Mars. Fictional elements (the student character Linh) are labelled as fiction.
Accuracy method: Every fact is linked to a source ID. We keep different milestones separate (last signal vs. official end of mission), flag uncertain items as needs_review, and use real NASA images with attribution instead of AI images as historical evidence. We cross-checked the Surveyor 3 comic against NASA Science, NSSDCA and JPL technical reports.
Technology: React 18, Tailwind CSS, Google model-viewer, deployed as a static site. Released under Apache-2.0.
Limitations: There is no backend in this version. Explorer Pass and gallery submissions are stored locally in the visitor's browser only, with no sharing or moderation. Next steps are a moderated shared gallery and more machines.
Benefits and goals: Give learners a story-first path into space history, make it accessible (bilingual, audio with transcript), and inspire the next generation of explorers.
Use of Super Intelligence (SI): Comic illustrations (Google Gemini / NotebookLM, visible SI watermark), the song "Little Wheels" (Suno), and parts of the website code ([tool names], used for coding and debugging) were SI-assisted or SI-generated. Research and data interpretation were assisted by SI and every historical fact was verified by the team against NASA sources. No NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers appear in SI-generated content.
